name: Killaloe Bridge
facts: Killaloe Bridge, a thirteen‑arch marvel, first appeared around 1650 and was rebuilt in 1825, then upgraded with a lifting section in 1929 to accommodate river traffic.
An ornate monument crowns the center of Killaloe Bridge, honoring four IRA members shot there in 1920 during the Irish War of Independence, while a plaque records its 1825 partial rebuild.
In 2025, a brand‑new Brian Boru Bridge opened just a kilometer south, but Killaloe Bridge remains a protected structure, listed by both Clare and Tipperary County Councils.
